summary: EC serial reassign after battery swap causes BitLocker unseal failures & provisioning hang
description:
Issue summary: Several depot-return laptops that underwent battery replacement (battery swap and EC firmware reflash step) are failing to finish post-repair provisioning. Symptoms: machines drop into BitLocker key protector prompt or Windows enter recovery screen, Autopilot/AAD join does not complete, and our agent stalls on 'finalizing device identity'.

Observed pattern: EC (embedded controller) serial number on some repaired units is being re-assigned to a different chassis serial in the asset DB during repair staging. The asset DB reconciliation process then flags a serial collision which triggers our provisioning agent to clear TPM owner state as part of a safety flow. That leads to BitLocker key protector mismatch and a recovery loop on first boot.

Why this matters: Blocks reprovisioning throughput at depot (~25-30% reprovision failure rate for battery-repaired builds this week), delays laptop return-to-service, increases manual intervention, and risks exposure of untracked asset state changes.
impact: Depot imaging stalls, ~20-30 machines affected this week in us-west depot. Manual recovery required for each unit. Increases repair lead time and costs. No customer-facing outage but internal SLA for RMA turnaround impacted.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Perform battery replacement and run depot staging image (includes EC firmware reflash tool v2.1.4)
2) Run asset-sync (depot tool) to update chassis/EC serials to central asset DB
3) Initiate Autopilot / Imaging task and reboot into Windows OOBE
4) Observe WMIC/sgfw outputs show EC serial differs from chassis serial in asset DB, asset-sync triggers a reconciliation path that marks duplicate=TRUE
5) Provisioning agent invokes TPM reset safety flow -> BitLocker protector mismatch -> Windows recovery screen
logs:
Excerpt of provisioning-agent log (timestamps normalized):
2026-03-09T09:11:23Z INFO starting asset-sync for host DELL-7440-AB12
2026-03-09T09:11:24Z WARN ec_serial 0x1A23F conflicts with asset-db chassis_serial 0x1A23F (owner: DEVICE-2982)
2026-03-09T09:11:24Z INFO reconciliation: flag_duplicate=true, invoking safety_reset_flow
2026-03-09T09:11:25Z INFO tpm_reset_requested by safety flow
2026-03-09T09:11:30Z ERROR bitlocker_unseal_failed keyprotector not found (status 0xE07)
2026-03-09T09:11:30Z ERROR provisioning halted - awaiting manual recovery
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: EC firmware reflash tool v2.1.4 writes an EC serial field that is non-unique (race or defaulting) leading to collisions in asset-sync.
Verified: two repaired units show identical EC serial bytes after reflash; original chassis serial unchanged in system BIOS. EC serial duplication only appears after reflash step.

Asset DB reconciliation logic currently treats any EC serial collision as authoritative and triggers TPM safety reset. This was intended for rare tamper cases but is too aggressive in depot repair flows.

Checked recent PRs: imaging-scripts PR-87 modified EC reflash step and introduced fallback default in case of flash failure; this may mask failure and set default serial to 0x1A23F. Linked PRs for review.
Repro locally in depot lab with synthetic EC flash -> duplicates are reproducible ~80% when flash fails fast-path and fallback executes.
Risk: current automatic TPM reset flow can cause BitLocker key protector loss if machine had encryption enabled before repair (common for enterprise fleet).
comments: Support (Daniel Kim) 2026-03-10: First reported by Depot Team when triage noticed two DELL units booting to recovery after battery swap. Attached logs and initial sample images.

SRE (Priya Menon) 2026-03-11: Confirmed duplication in lab. Repro steps documented. Pausing automatic TPM safety_reset in asset-sync to avoid further incidents (temporary mitigation deployed to us-west depot only).

Firmware Eng (Lena Ortiz) 2026-03-11: Investigating EC reflash tool. Found code path that writes fallback serial 0x1A23F on verification failures. Preparing PR to abort and surface explicit failure instead of writing fallback.

Policy (Aaron Lee) 2026-03-12: Noted that asset-sync reconciliation policy was intended to be conservative for tamper detection. Recommend adding depot-repair exception flag based on vendor repair token.
Depot Lead (Marta Silva) 2026-03-12: Requesting runbook entries for manual recovery and guidance for technicians when encountering this state.
Security (Oliver Grant) 2026-03-12: Concern about disabling TPM safety flows; acceptable as temporary mitigation only if logging/audit preserved.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: asset-sync updated in us-west depot to treat 'depot_repair_token' annotated requests as low-confidence duplicates and skip automatic TPM reset. Firmware team opened PR to stop writing fallback EC serial in reflash tool (PR-412). Full rollout pending QA. Manual recovery runbook created and circulated to depot techs.
next_steps: 1) Merge firmware fix PR to abort flash instead of writing fallback serial (owner: Lena Ortiz, target: 2026-03-15)
2) Update asset-sync reconciliation to add repair-token-aware policy and add explicit audit events (owner: SRE, target: 2026-03-14)
3) QA of changed flows in staging depot (owner: Depot QA, target: 2026-03-16)
4) Backfill audit and run a cross-check job to detect any previously mis-assigned EC serials and remediate (owner: AssetDB team, target: 2026-03-18)
5) Follow-up postmortem and update depot runbook with recovery steps and detection heuristics (owner: Operations, target: 2026-03-20)
